correctness.rationale: For the exact probability measure and harmonic monomial orthonormal basis, angular Fourier orthogonality gives the full action of T_{z^N} and the telescoped action of (T_z)^N. Their difference is supported on exactly N-1 disjoint input/output basis pairs. Strict covariance of X^j and X^(N-j) gives positive, nonzero singular coefficients. The increasing beta-moment ratios force the exact central maximizing index. Gamma-ratio asymptotics uniform on compact bulk intervals plus bounded endpoint contributions rigorously give the distribution, exact operator-norm limit, all Schatten exponents p>0 and quantile limit. The standalone checker independently tests exact rational Toeplitz coefficient identities and supplementary limits, but is not substituted for infinite mathematical proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the entire singular spectrum and a high-power beta-profile/Schatten asymptotic for a growing-length monomial Toeplitz product on weighted harmonic Bergman spaces. The three directly relevant full-text primary sources establish respectively spectra of individual polynomial-symbol operators, fixed two-factor product criteria, and fixed two-factor finite-rank canonical forms; none gives the growing-power singular distribution or all-p limits. The closest published quantitative records concern different operator families or different observables. The finite-rank property is background, not claimed as the novel achievement. This is a best-knowledge conclusion with the specific literature risks recorded below.
residual_risks: An earlier equivalent growing-degree spectral law might be embedded implicitly in shift-operator or Toeplitz power literature under alternative terminology.

Fixed-degree formulas for unweighted two-factor semicommutators are established by Dong–Zhou (2014); the novelty assertion is restricted to the weighted variable-power singular distribution and sharp all-p asymptotic.

value.rationale: The natural defect measures failure of the analytic monomial compression to preserve multiplicative powers. Each defect is square-zero finite rank, yet its norm does not decay and its rank grows; the new exact beta singular profile and all-p sharp constants quantify this failure for the entire natural family of beta weights. The result is a complete spectral distribution rather than an arbitrary finite slice or numerical increment, and distinguishes fixed-degree rank classifications from a genuinely variable-power spectral law.
